sentences.text: This dinosaur reached a length of approximately 4.8 meters and a mass of 265 kilograms.
Other estimates suggest it measured about 4.5 meters long and weighed 250 kilograms.
It is distinguished by possessing strong, long forelimbs that exceeded 65 centimeters in length, a feature often reduced in other theropods.
The hand retained four metacarpals, and the shoulder blade featured a distinct acromial prominence unlike the flattened glenoid region seen in other theropods.
The species Xuanhanosaurus qilixiaensis was named by Dong Zhiming in 1984.
The fossil specimen was recovered in 1979 during a dinosaur survey in Sichuan Province.
The holotype specimen IVPP V.6729 was found in the Lower Shaximiao Formation in China.
This holotype consists of a partial skeleton lacking a skull, including a scapula, coracoid, possible sternum, forelimb bones, and some dorsal vertebrae.
Researchers suggest the strong arms of Xuanhanosaurus may have been used for catching prey.
Recent work indicates Xuanhanosaurus retains ceratosaurian-like short phalanges similar to those found in Saltriovenator.
Most studies agree that Xuanhanosaurus is a tetanuran, possibly a basal allosauroid, notable for retaining a vestigial fourth metacarpal.
Dong originally assigned Xuanhanosaurus to Megalosauridae and considered it a middle-stage tetanuran due to its vestigial fourth metacarpal.
In 2009, Roger Benson found Xuanhanosaurus belonged to a primitive lineage of Megalosauroidea.
In 2018, it was argued that Xuanhanosaurus belongs to early-diverging branches of the ceratosaurian-tetanuran node based on features like the vestigial fourth metacarpal.
In 2019, Rauhut and Pol placed Xuanhanosaurus outside Metriacanthosauridae as the basalmost member of Allosauroidea.
The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Xuanhanosaurus as Piatnitzkysauridae.

Xuanhanosaurus lived in the Sichuan Basin, China, during the Middle Jurassic (Bathonian) approximately 166 million years ago, while other sources place it in the Middle Jurassic Callovian stage between 167 and 161 million years ago.

Xuanhanosaurus lived in what is now Asia during the Middle Jurassic Callovian stage, between 167 and 161 million years ago, whereas other estimates suggest it lived during the Middle Jurassic (Bathonian) approximately 166 million years ago.

It is debated whether Xuanhanosaurus walked on four legs; while the describer suggested it was the only known four-legged meat-eater, later paleontologists argue it walked on hind legs because arm pronation was impossible.
